title: Notifications with actions never close upon expiry even when they don't go to history
line: Notifications with buttons that won't be kept in the history now tell their app they closed when the popup times out.
explanation: When the popup of a notification with actions timed out, Plasma only marked it as expired so it would stay usable from the history, and the sending app got no NotificationClosed until it quit. This also happened to notifications that never show up in the history: apps without a desktop entry (the default "@other" setting has Show in history off), apps or services with Show in history turned off, and low urgency ones. Apps waiting for the close signal, like the reporter's, waited forever. The popup now mirrors the history model's filter (including the "@other" fallback) and expires such notifications like any other.

commits.message:
applets/notifications: Expire popups with actions not kept in history

Notifications with actions were only marked as expired so they stay usable
in the history, even when they never reach it, so their senders waited for
NotificationClosed forever. Mirror the history filter and expire those.

BUG: 506633

patches.diff:
From 50dc366b0e93f30191a5b522c40618248a1ce00c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:18:47 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/notifications: Expire popups with actions not kept in
 history

Notifications with actions were only marked as expired so they stay usable
in the history, even when they never reach it, so their senders waited for
NotificationClosed forever. Mirror the history filter and expire those.

BUG: 506633
---
 applets/notifications/global/Globals.qml | 10 ++++++++--
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/applets/notifications/global/Globals.qml b/applets/notifications/global/Globals.qml
index 8e8e56f88d..2fbe8f91bd 100644
--- a/applets/notifications/global/Globals.qml
+++ b/applets/notifications/global/Globals.qml
@@ -526,6 +526,11 @@ QtObject {
 
             readonly property bool isTransient: model.transient // "transient" is a reserved keyword, cannot declare it as required property
             readonly property bool hasSomeActions: hasDefaultAction || (actionLabels).length > 0 || (configureActionLabel).length > 0 || hasReplyAction
+            // Mirrors the filter of the history model in main.qml, non-configurable notifications use the "@other" settings entry
+            readonly property string settingsDesktopEntry: !desktopEntry && !configurable && type === NotificationManager.Notifications.NotificationType ? "@other" : desktopEntry
+            readonly property bool keptInHistory: (urgency !== NotificationManager.Notifications.LowUrgency || globals.notificationSettings.lowPriorityHistory)
+                && !(settingsDesktopEntry && globals.notificationSettings.historyBlacklistedApplications.includes(settingsDesktopEntry))
+                && !(notifyRcName && globals.notificationSettings.historyBlacklistedServices.includes(notifyRcName))
 
             popupWidth: globals.popupWidth
             showPopupTimeout: globals.notificationSettings.showPopupTimeout
@@ -667,11 +672,12 @@ QtObject {
 
             onHoverEntered: model.read = true
             onExpired: {
-                if (resident || (hasSomeActions && !isTransient)) {
+                if (resident || (hasSomeActions && !isTransient && keptInHistory)) {
                     // When resident, only mark it as expired so the popup disappears
                     // but don't actually invalidate the notification.
                     // Also don't invalidate if the popup has any actions,
-                    // so it remains usable in history, except when explicitly transient.
+                    // so it remains usable in history, except when explicitly transient
+                    // or when it won't show up in the history at all.
                     model.expired = true;
                 } else {
                     globals.popupNotificationsModel.expire(globals.popupNotificationsModel.index(index, 0))
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Before: app 'Nyx' (no desktop entry) sends a notification with a Test button and a 1.5 s timeout
Before: the popup is gone and nothing is in the history, yet the app got no NotificationClosed in 15 s
After: the popup is gone and the app receives NotificationClosed (reason 1, expired) at 1.5 s

review.text: Right fix for the remaining case: notifications that will never reach the history now expire properly, so the sender gets NotificationClosed. The '@other' mapping that the earlier branch missed is now included. The history filter is duplicated in QML (it already exists in main.qml and in C++ in notifications.cpp), so the two can drift apart. Exposing a 'kept in history' helper from libnotificationmanager would be cleaner, but this is acceptable as is.
